simple.meaning: זֶרֶם (zerem) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a gush of water.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 24:8. The surrounding context includes mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זֶרֶם (H2230) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H2230. zerem זֶ֫רֶם noun masculine Hab 3:10 flood of rain, rain-storm, downpour (Aramaic זַרְמִית id. ) — absolute ׳ז Isa 4:6 2 t.; זָ֑רֶם 32:2 ; construct זֶרֶם Job 24:8 4 t.; Isa 4:6 (|| מָטָר )); ׳ז מַיִם 28:2 ; Hab 3:10 ; ׳ז הָרִים Job 24:8 , i.e. such as falls among mountains compare Di; ׳ז בָּרָד Isa 28:2 ; מִזֶּרֶם מַחְסֶה 25:4 , קִיר זֶרֶם 25:4 i.e. such as dashes against a wall, 32:2 (|| רוּחַ ), בָּרָד וְאֶבֶן וָזֶרֶם נֶפֶץ 30:30 .

occurrences.englishText: They are wet with the showers of the mountains,
There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.

For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.

For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
Behold, the Lord has a mighty and strong one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will cast them down to the earth with his hand.
Behold, the Lord has a mighty and strong one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will cast them down to the earth with his hand.
Yahweh will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind,
The mountains saw you, and were afraid.
